t: It looks like the expedition leader recorded a holographic message. It was the right thing to do, very fortunate for us. Shall we listen?
Find out what happened to the party on the lower levels of the Citadel

I suggest you don't focus on finding the whole expedition. You want to find certain members, namely, Imperius. The probability of their survival was zero a week ago. Nobody knows what awaits you downstairs, so carefully consider your every step. This place is much more dangerous than it looks.
If you intend to continue your investigation, the portal in front of me will take you straight to the bowels of the Citadel.
Wonderful. I wasn't wrong - this enterprise will be beneficial for us both.
Listen to what Imperius has to say.

Destroyers have nothing to do with the device. At least, I sensed no energy of theirs down there. I only heard the call... The call of our fallen Progenitor Sarn.

This device used to belong to a god. I don't know what it's really meant for. And I don't want to know! This place makes me sick. No good can happen here.
This place makes me sick. No good can happen here.

Thank you once again for your help down there. If it weren't for you, we all would have died, not just... not just Alastar.

As for the stone in the device... I want you to keep it. I'm sure you can make better use of it than I, let alone the locals.

The stone was an artifact core. Its properties... are scaring me.

Farewell, Stormbringer. I hope I will see you again.
Teleport to the Sogot Citadel and ask Tegorah for advice.

You'd better leave the demonologists alone. Demons trust you, ask them for advice. You may talk to Tegorah directly, I guess.

Give my regards to the big guy. He's a decent fellow, even though he's a demon.
...Tegorah falls silent for a while. Obviously, it isn't the best day for a friendly visit. Skulnar's regards can wait.

Tegorah turns away. His voice is unambiguously venomous.

Ask sorceress Maya for advice. She and her gang willingly betray anyone and point at the guilty. If she knows anyone that fits your description, she will turn them in without second though. She owes you.
Oh, it's you again. Welcome back. What brought you here?
Oh, it's you again. Welcome back. What brought you here?

Mind control? I'm afraid you have come to the wrong person. Studying something that has been studied thoroughly by generations of psionicists is useless. You could go straight to them without wasting my time.

If you're interested, though... One of my subordinates, aoidos Imperius, is using the data in question in his research. He's a member of the expedition to the Citadel's deepest levels. It's been a month since they departed.

Speaking of which... you might have arrived just in time.
I'm very busy. Leave me alone.
I wish we had copies of Imperius's research... Every demonologist keeps their knowledge secret. Your only option is to find him yourself. You have my permission for an expedition.
Meet Nogrom Junior at the workshop

The purpose of the expedition? This is absolutely none of your business. Everything in the name of science. No surprises here. All you should know is that your destination is in the depths of the Citadel. Perhaps, they're waiting for you to save them.

Why don't we go? Out of the question. The Church is following our every step. There's still risk of the Destroyers' attack. The demons have been acting weirdly and aggressively. Every demonologist counts here. We're saving ourselves, you know.

During a fight with the Destroyers the passage that the expedition took was destroyed. Your goblin was supposed to research a different option to bring them back. You can ask him about the progress. And please, make sure he doesn't blow up what is not supposed to be blown up.

Hey, chief! I did nothing illegal!

Nope. Nothing illegal at all!

Hey, chief! I did nothing illegal!

Nope. Nothing illegal at all!
Search trails of the Expedition on the lower levels.

Let's put aside the possibility of an incident. Suppose they were attacked. But by whom?

Demons? A riot means genocide for them. It does not contribute to their goals, anyway. And I doubt that a bunch of renegade demons could make a big part of the expedition.

Demonologists? Who could benefit from the death of the whole expedition? We will have to check all members... Survivors, if there are any, are automatically under suspicion. Beware, Stormbringer.

Continue your descent. The solution is near.
Continue your descent. The solution is near.

Demon's movements are smooth and precise. You don't feel a direct threat, but his gestures betray not only an experienced sorcerer, but and experienced assassin.

I didn't expect to see you here, Stormbringer. Your Spark is shining in the dark too bright. I wonder if there is a way to dim it.
...Some bloody bandages. Someone from the advance party must have been wounded. There isn't too much blood. The wound wasn't bad.
Go through the dark creatures with Alastar's help.

...Demon's manner of speech takes you by surprise. You don't often see a demon attempting at humor. However, he becomes serious again.

We need to take you away from here. Now that you're here, Imperius has a chance to escape. We might have it too.

You can call me Alastar. I'm... a friend of Imperius.

...A suspicious noise in the dark interrupts the demon. He lowers his head, listens carefully to the noises in the corners, in the corridors, among stone plates. You can feel the anxiety and unease building up.

I will try and summon the Light, Stormbringer. Stay close. Run if I die. Your life is more important. I will take you to Imperius.

It came as a surprise! The first pleasant surprise during the last month. Well done, Alastar!

Stormbringer, is it? It's wonderful! It's amazing!
...You can't read demon's face as he's looking at you. His spirit is clearly emanating tranquility.

h: Tell Alastar that you're ready to go.

t:
I knew Terminus would find a way to get through to me. But sending Stormbringer to help! He outdid himself, ha-ha!

I told him about our problem via the mental link we're keeping. It's just, you know... We were in a stalemate. If a few demons and I returned save and sound, it would have raised some questions. And we would have been forced to tell what lies in the depths of the Citadel.

We could have long summoned help. But we can't let demonologist arrive here.

Now that Alastar and I are able to preserve our minds, your power, and Terminus's knowledge, we've got a chance! What we don't have is time.

Let's do it.
Glad to see you, although we haven't met.

Well, the task is clear. Magotriangulation in a place like this can be greatly hampered by noise, but at least the streams from the upper levels will not interfere in the picture.

The A.I.D. has all beacons you need for the operation. You must install them properly. Like this...

In your position, I would be prepared for... unpleasant surprises. Who knows what hides in the dark. We are only at the very tip of the iceberg.

Good luck!
In your position, I would be prepared for... unpleasant surprises. Who knows what hides in the dark. We are only at the very tip of the iceberg.

The picture is not very clear. But the source is unmistakable, for it's very powerful. What is that noise?

You'd better hurry, Stormbringer. You shouldn't sit around expecting someone else's orders. We have... What we have here... There's some unrest. I'm sorry, it's hard for me to think. Protection of Imperius and Alastar doesn't apply to me. I'm not physically present.

The good news is that the source is not far from here. The bad news is that it's completely cut off from the main structure. The whole room is isolated from the Citadel, so to say. So it's near, and at the same time, it's very difficult to access. The architectural paradox easily achieved by adepts of dimensional magic. I wonder for how long it's been here...

However, we can use the teleportation network of the Citadel to enter. In fact, it's the bad news. You will have only a few moments to evaluate the situation and defend yourself if necessary.

Stay alert.
Let's go. It's time to put an end to it.

I don't feel so good. What is this construction?

It looks like a device.
There's so much energy around, the air is buzzing!

In a normal situation, I'm not a fan of scientific vandalism, but I'm afraid we'll have to destroy the artifact before we can study it. I don't know about you, Stormbringer, but my thoughts are scaring me. I can see only... the red... the black. The black light...

Please, do something! Make it stop!
Please, do something! Make it stop!

No... No! Alastar! Can you hear me?

Say something! Alastar...
Go to Frontier with the Centaurs through Sculptor's Portal

An intriguing option. Life here is relatively not diverse, but you can find traces of many lost civilizations of this world.

I will open the way for us.
I can see that these lands are vast, but the fact that we arrived at the middle of the burned wasteland spoils the impression.

I can feel life. There must be a settlement. We are guests on this land, we must pay a visit to its residents.

Stay alert. We don't know their reaction.

Funny outlanders! Why take horse's body? Hey, the stone idol walks!

Ooh, Lizardman remember you! You kill all Draconids! May their name be cursed forever.

We have holy days. Celebration! Can't spill blood. Even outlander's blood. You are double luck today! Our home be your home.
Find Kiela, the missing daughter of the chief, in Waterfolk village.

Want find home here? Earth is big! Burning Claw is happy to have friends! My daughter Kiela wants make friends with Waterfolk. Went to them a moon ago. Never come back. I begin worry.

You want see our land? See the Waterfolk land, too. If you find Kiela, tell her come back. Tell her, Hiss Abyss wait!
Not so good. Why those people capture them? Slave traders? What does this mean?
They... they attacked! Captured everyone! Took them away!..
Free the captives and get rid of pirates, the slave traders.

No honor... Even a life of an enemy is precious. Humiliate enemy, you humiliate yourself. Citovras was teaching this! Selling outlanders like stone necklaces is...

Dishonorable.

Unworthy death to the dishonored! Kill them like wild dogs!

Praise the Claw! The Fiery Sky sent you! Mercy on our life! Wrath on unworthy intruder! What? Not Sky? Father sent you? My father is the chief! Sky talks through him!

If the silly Waterfolk stop squeaking at each other, we could have done it! Harr!
Support the peace treaty between the Lakefolk, the Riverfolk, and the Burning Claw tribe.

Two tribes, Riverfolk and Lakefolk. It's a loooong war.

Today it ends! I, Kiela, the daughter of the chief, will talk!
Thank you, Outlander! One stupid war over. We are strong tribe. We must make peace on our land.
Join the celebration of the Burning Claw tribe.

Outlander bring luck! Stay, Outlander. We have a big feast tonight!

Hissit-Asha-Shi, the great spirit, talk to me in shaman's dream. He invite you. Very persistent. He say, you're lost in the dark. He wants to help.

Let the horse stay, too. And the statue. Let's celebrate with the Claw!

Good morning!

Hiss Abyss says, their patron blessed you last night. He's right. Something has changed about you.

Spirits are with you, Stormbringer. This is good.
Collect Poisonous Kelp from the bottom of the lake.

Our tribe wants to make a gift to the Burning Claw chief to thank them for saving our lives. Poisonous kelp is growing on the bottom of the lake. Applied to weapons, it makes them deadly!

If only my Lakefolk could collect it... They're too tired after the battle with the pirates!

Please, help us once again. But be cautious. This kelp exhales poison. Don't approach if you can see a green cloud around a plant.

Great kelp! Are you okay? Alive? Good.

Give it to me, I'll process it...

Our tribe would like to make a return gift to the Burning Claw chief as a token of our gratitude and unity.

We are giving you wonderful and shiny Royal Crab Shells!
This shell is sturdy and beautiful. It can make a good armor for a hunter. Or a sharp spear.

Glug. Glug. Friend! Help me out, please?

Our lake, Eldress, is full of delicious crabs, but they are very dangerous for us Waterfolk. You get distracted, and bam - a crab chops off your hand. It takes a long time to regenerate one! Who will feed my kids?

Catch us these crabs, since you are a great hero! And you've proven it time and time again. We will compose a song about you and sing it to the children.
Excellent! We'll use everything. Shells for armor and weapons, meat - for food! Thank you.
Return to the Burning Claw chief together with Kiela and Ancient Moon
We discuss laws of our union, and everybody is made happy. Have something to tell father and the tribe. Let's go now. Water and kelp make my scales itch.

Kiela! My baby!

You're alive! Praise the Burning Claw! An the outlanders, too.

It is a magnificent land, Stormbringer.

I hope, it will stay this way. Hiss Abyss and his tribe are glorious... what do they call themselves? Lizardmen? Their shaman traditions are very curious. Thank you for the opportunity to get to know them.

It's a shame, but it's time to say our good-byes.

It was an amazing journey. The world is so huge and diverse... It is so much grander than all this fussing about...

However minor, these things are important enough for our lives to depend on it. That's the fate.
Go to Gipat Shard with the Centaurs through Sculptor's Portal.
Gipat Shard. The source of the Dark God's revelation. This land is full of energy, although it isn't pure. It's rather easy to make way there.

Darkness and fog... These lands are so much unlike the Spiral Ridge.

But they look vast and deserted. Let's look around.
Go up the Ruins together with the Centaurs.

If we climb these ruins, we can see the land for many miles around, as the fog allows... I think I can see a ladder over there.

Let's go! We must see what this land has to offer.

Strangers can't go any further. Talk to the chief if you don't value your life, huh.

There he is.

So, it's you, then. Huh, the Wind told me you would come. I don't know what the Mountain spirits see in you, but their will is absolute. The Trial of Power awaits you!

You will fight against my sons. I have two, so you may select the opponent. There's only one rule. You can't go out of the circle.

Fight till death!

Oh, it's not up to the ancestral testament... We will be punished for the defiance!

On the other hand... we haven't heard the ancestral voices in a long time. They are silent. Shaman's visions are dark.
Listen to what Spinecrusher has to say.

Perhaps, this is why the wind of Gipat blew you in.

The woe came to our tribe... You may be our salvation!

The ancestors have long abandoned us. But we're alive so far, and we're not going to die!

Your shaman is strong and wise. The two of you are mighty warriors. Strangers brought woe to us. Only strangers should know how to deal with it. That's what the wind is telling us.
Install the Mountain Wind's Staff at the foot of the ruins and kill several ghostly toads and boars in the circle.

Well, we don't owe them anything, but I have a bad feeling about this place. I must figure out what's going on.

If it's about the ancestral spirits, we should try asking other spirits' advice. Here, take my staff. Use it to trap spirits at the foot of the ruins. Use it on ghostly toads and boars.

At the moment of death, the staff must be near the creature. Don't forget it.

Whatever it is, they're not real spirits. I can see you know this darkness. I've seen it in my dreams beyond the forbidden boundary.

I didn't let it come closer.

Have the spirits ever been alive? Or it's just an evil illusion? I do not know...

I just fear that the Orcish "Spirits of the Ancestors" are nothing but darkness.

And still, I was able to see something. A strange cave filled with darkness. Something light was locked inside it, tied with magic chains. If we find the cave, we'll find the answer.

I've seen the path surrounded by stone pillars with rainbow lightning dancing around them. We must find this place.
Find the Cursed Path on Gipat Shard.

I know this place. I can see it in your eyes that you know it, too. It's the Cursed Path. That's what it's called by the crazy human ghosts from the village.

We are staying away from it. The rainbow lightning burns down everyone on the spot, and no offerings can help. I don't think the spirits have any power over the stone pillars at all.

But if the shaman says that you have to take it... So be it.
Wait, Stormbringer. This path is dangerous. We may die if we proceed without protection.
Walk along the Cursed Path under shaman's protection.

This element has nothing to do with the nature or spirits. It is dark magic. There is no rainbow lightning, Stormbringer. There is only darkness... only the black light...

I think I can protect us, but we must walk quickly.

Yes, this is the cave. What's inside?

I'm... I'm scared, Stormbringer.
Enter the cave and defeat the darkness inside.

I have a bad feeling. Whatever hides inside, it's very powerful. And it's somehow connected with this land, like the Well of Souls is connected with Ammer.

Now I know why I feel so bad on this allod.

Stormbringer, resisting the darkness is our sacred duty! If orcs are going to survive, they must get rid of such neighbor.

We banished the dark creation!

The ancestral spirits helped us. They were imprisoned here. It's so good to know that they didn't become a part of the evil.

It's just... the spirits are very weak. I can feel them fading slowly, but steadily.

I think they want to tell us something. Hurry, Stormbringer, listen carefully before their quiet words are carried away by the wind.

You are the Chosen One, and for a reason. What you did for us is worthy of all treasure in the world.

We must carefully learn the last lesson of the ancestors. The dark times begin... Time will show if we are worthy of survival.

I wish you and the Spiral Ridge tribe to find whatever you are looking for.

Go in peace, Chosen One. My sons and I will stay here a little longer.

Our adventure in Gipat is coming to an end. This land belongs to the orcs, and they wished to face their destiny. We're leaving these lands now. It's time to return, Stormbringer. The Stone God will open the gates.
Welcome back. I hope your research was productive.
Teleport to Wellebell Preserve via Sculptor's Portal

Umoir? Hmm, the chaos in this land was particularly bad. The Leper, that's what you named it.

Now the Leper is growing weaker. Local residents continue to explore their territory. I'm not sure it would be wise to visit them right now, but it's up to you to decide.
They aren't happy about our arrival. I understand that. A tragedy at your door makes you appreciate your home.
Explore Wellebell Preserve together with the Centaurs.

The wish of the people is commendable. We are not claiming their land.

But it is amazing! Since we've only got one day, let's go as deep as we can. Some special energy is filling this place.

I want to see its history with my own eyes.
Just to think that it's only a little fragment of the world... After the Leper, it's a sorry sight...
Gather acorns and berries for Mountain Wind.

The Earth can tell you a lot about itself through its gifts. I wonder which of local herbs and berries are edible.

I can manage the herbs. In the meantime, bring me some red berries that are all over this place. And the big seeds of these huge trees.

What do you call them? Acorns? Yes, bring me acorns!
Excellent. Who knows, maybe these seeds will grow on Ammer.

Citovras used to say, a good warrior must be brave, strong, and sate.

My belly is almost empty with all these adventures. I'd rather guard my sister. Who knows what beasts live here! In the meantime, bring us a boar for dinner. No, make it five!

We'll eat one right here and bring the rest to our brothers at the Spiral Ridge. It's no good returning from travels without gifts.
Uh, some roasted boar meat would make this place feel like home...
That's a surprise! Boar piglets are almost exactly the same as we have. It's a shame.

Honor and valor!

My brothers, the centaurs of the Spiral Ridge, liked the local wild boars… Damn, they taste amazing, especially honey-dipped ribs.

So here it is: you need to kill enough boars to feed everyone. As for the locals - I don't think they would mind - there's plenty of pigs here.

So - be a friend, get us some meat! And we will arrange a feast in your honor.
Oh, hunting is great here in these forests!
Excellent! As Citovras said, "there is nothing like the good food we'll eat, glorious beer we'll drink, and a hot mare we'll..." ahem, we will omit this part!
These lands were devastated during the war with the Leper. Have people won it? Umoir people are mighty... Citovras taught us to respect those who lived through troubles.
...Ancient Moon frowns and growls even in his sleep. He might be dreaming about the fight by the Well of Souls and the brave tribe chieftain.
...The shaman cuddles the magic staff in her sleep.
Capture a squirrel for Ancient Moon.

Citovras said that a true warrior must not be ashamed of their desires. So.

Well...

While we walked through the forest, I noticed some red-furred creatures up in the trees and on the ground... Squirrels? Huh. I wonder if they're soft to the touch... I'd love to pat one!

Do me a favor, catch one for me! Make sure you don't cripple it. Use a bait.
So, how is it going with the squirrel?

It's so fluffy and gentle!

You know, there are so many of them! One more squirrel, one less...

I'll keep this one. And I'm going to name it... let me see...
Go to sleep by the fire.

It was a good day, Stormbringer. The sun is declining. It's time for a rest.

Go to sleep. Look, we have a wolf skin for you. What's with the suspicion? Are you afraid to sleep? Don't worry, Stormbringer. No one can harm you in this forest.

Good night.

Good morning, Stormbringer!

We are ready to go home now.
Tell Mountain Wind about your dream.
I've seen weird things in my dream... Did you sleep well? I tried to protect you from darkness in your thoughts, but...
Keep the Sage's gift, Stormbringer. Something tells me you'll find it useful.
Summon the Sculptor and teleport to Ammer with Centaurs.

It's time to return, Stormbringer. The Stone God told us to summon him, whenever we're ready.

He gave me this thing, but I have no clue how to use it. Please, use it to summon the Stone God and return home.
The teleportation was successful. Welcome back!
Explore Wellebell Preserve, Gipat Shard, and Frontier together with the Centaurs.

The new life form desires to start an expansion? I must express fear that they will face the fate of the Architects who began their expansion into this world earlier.

"Absolutely different?" Probably.

I can open portals to your destinations to optimize your travel. Navigating in this ocean of chaos is so fascinating.
The long journey is over. The answer to my question is ready.

It was a wonderful journey. I had no idea our world was so beautiful and huge... After all, there are many lands yet to be seen.

The Sculptor is willing to help on one condition. Our expansion must be peaceful. Well, that's something I can promise!

Allow me to give our decision to the tribe. This is the grand occasion for us, Centaurs. It wouldn't have happened if it weren't for your help.
Thank you for everything you've done, Stormbringer. You will always be welcome here and in our future home on Frontier.

Sarn is dead, but his legacy is still kicking, hah. I'm pretty sure we'll have to interrogate our diving Terrorwing.

I have no clue where this Sculptor might be now. Klavdia is supposed to keep an eye on him. You should ask her.
Do you really need the Sculptor?

Let me guess, you need the Sculptor to save the world, right?

Ah, is it just your soul? How boring! Well, if you insist...
Capture the Eye of the Sculptor and bring it to Klavdia.

I have an idea. The aoidos say that strange small creatures appeared here. They're somehow related, but in fact they belong to another world. The Sculptor is hanging out somewhere, letting out lots of his little friends! Catch one of them. It's going to tell us everything we need to know.

Here's a special trap for Architects. It isn't finished, so it overheats quickly. Make sure you set it at the right moment.
Well, he's a hard case! Do you know where he is? Visiting the Spiral Ridge! Do you get where the wind is blowing?
Find a way into the Centaur Camp at the Spiral Ridge and find the Sculptor.

I swear to the Balance, if this pathetic idol starts another cult... Oh, he must be stopped! Although... you didn't get along with centaurs very well the last time I remember. I hope you will manage to find common grounds with them after... well, after you killed their beloved chieftain!
Greetings and welcome back, Child of Chaos. My scout informed me that you were looking for me. What happened?
Speak to Apios and get to the Centaur Camp.

Greetings and welcome back, Stormbringer! I don't have much news. Everything is in order. After the death of Kyros and Citovras, the aoidos and Centaurs made peace. No one wants any more blood. The Triquetrum is free again! Find Apios in Triquetrum, he'll be happy to see you.
Since you're looking for the Stone God, go and talk to him. He can't find common ground with my sister.
Good to see you again, Stormbringer!
As you can see, we made peace with the Centaurs. Both nations believe that we are too small and, how shall I put it, too mortal to be involved in a war for territory.
h: How are the things going in Triquetrum?

t:
Ha! How about taking that canyon after you've covered yourself in sticky stinky... phew. Let's not get into that. They should have closed that backdoor, anyway.

We have peace, but the Centaurs are not prepared to open the gates of their camp for us. They might let you come in, though. Centaurs respect power. My friend Ancient Moon will show you the way.

I'm sorry I can't keep you company. Too busy. Triquetrum is growing by the hour.
h: How can I get to the Centaur Camp?

t: The cult? No, I don't want it. Unlike chaos creations, I learn from my mistakes. Dane's experience shows that chaos creations are too... sensitive to be my followers. I hope you know what I mean.
So you're the hero of the aoidos, Stormbringer. My dream was ominous. Amazing is spiritual knowledge! I'm happy to greet you in our camp.
Come with me, Stormbringer. I will tell you what awaits the Centaurs.

Wind told me that the Stone God and the lost soul will help us along the way. You don't look like a lost soul, but something troubles you. You didn't come here by chance.

The spirits promised that the lost soul would be rewarded for help. They said something about the Luminary to dispel darkness... I didn't quite get what they were saying.

What do you say, Stormbringer? Will you help us?

It saddens me to hear that innocent people suffer from the actions of those who live in the same world as I do.

The inhabitants of Eden do not deserve to be threatened with weapons and have their resources stolen. After all, they didn’t do us any harm, they didn’t even know we existed until recently.
h: Tell them what you have managed to learn in Eden

t: Use Klavdia's help to enter trance.

I can immerse you in a magic dream, where you will act consciously. Be warned that things and creatures in your dream will make little sense. There are neither enemies nor allies... Except for Darkness. By default, it is neither a foe nor a friend. It's up to you to decide what it will be. More precisely, to your subconscious.

What's wrong? Oh, I should have known better than to confuse you.

Just remember one thing. Everything that happens in the dream is your subconscious attempt to sort out the mess in your head. If it works out, you can find... I don't know what. Answers? Direction? Solution? More questions? I really don't know.

If something goes wrong, I will wake you up. But for your own good, pray to all gods for it to go right.

Just remember one thing. Everything that happens in the dream is your subconscious attempt to sort out the mess in your head. If it works out, you can find... I don't know what. Answers? Direction? Solution? More questions? I really don't know.

The face looks like a reflection in a distorted mirror. It looks puzzled and empty. It's studying you as closely as you're studying it.

This face looks familiar.
Try to establish contact with the creature in front of you.

...Your head is spinning, and the world around you crumbles. You realize that you're seeing yourself through the eyes of the strange ghost. A second later, its face reappears in front of you. It repeats again and again. Spin, glance, spin. You-he-you feel...s dizzy, and everything rolls back like ocean waves. Where I am and where IT is - becomes incomprehensible.

Suddenly, BOTH of you realize what's going on. The question is in order. It's the law. Ask the question. Receive the answer. No question, no life.
I'm asleep. I'm dreaming about a baby mouse, running away from my claws. The baby mouse knows how to play.

Why am I seeing you in my dream, baby mouse? You have all paths in the world ahead of you. You've got the lock and the key, but you can't see them. What a shame.

You know the rules, baby mouse. Answers are given to those, who ask questions. I know the rules. My dream, my questions. You reply to me, and you reply to yourself.

Maybe...

The reflection looks more confident. Strong. Just like you.

There's no more I-it-you-we thing. You are real. I am real. Keep going.
...The face before you is expecting your questions. The laws of intelligence are absolute.
The old man in dark clothes is smiling kindly at you. His face looks slightly familiar.
See? It's easier than it seems.
Enter the Portal of Eternity and see what happens.

You have asked the question, my friend. You know the rules! You will have your answer, ready or not.

Open the last door.

This is it... The journey is over.

Look at me.

I do know how. All signs, both mental and external, were present. I should know better...

What to do? Well, for starters, you can surrender to goblins on the Coba Plateau and wait for the local innkeeper to hire a minor local hero to rescue you. Then you must persuade a naive time-traveler to give you the heart of the Dragon, deeply roasted in the desert sands. Or, as an option, you may find an ancient half-witted mage and absorb the power of his Spark...

Or we can go the long way, get into your mind and cut the darkness out directly. You will do it yourself. I'm not messing with your thoughts.

Well? What would you choose?
We shall start as soon as you're ready, dear. Don't let it take too long. It's just like toothache.

Well, you did it. You did something.

Oh, I can see a lot of questions in your eyes. Have I come through this? Have I seen this? Do I know the "sacred" truth about Nihaz?

But of course.
Talk to Skulnar the Fierce in the Al Rihat Ruins.

Well, you can't escape from Darkness. The only way to escape is to accept it. To see the vanity and the necessity of fighting it. Everything is exactly as they said. Darkness is the natural state of the world. Darkness is the Great Uncertainty.

Speaking about Nihaz... Like Darkness, he has multiple faces. He is only one of its countless sides. His conflict with Sarn is only a minor episode in his long, unbearably long life. We are just one of the myriad tiniest consequences of this conflict.

It's true, we call the ghostly Umoir peasants, the lost Sculptor, and Nihaz "Gods", but only because we lack a proper word. Nihaz, how should I put it... Is more of a concept. An idea.

Yes, I think he is. The concept of a conflict. The idea of war. Did you think that gods of war must be huge, furious, menacing? Uh. I guess Nihaz has long outgrown this image. On the other hand, if you remember Thalos...

What does it make me as Nihaz's daughter? Hm. You should know better than anyone what is born in a war... Anyway, it doesn't really matter.

Skulnar wanted to talk to you. He's gripping on you so hard... It's no surprise. Go.
So the ginger head helped you, after all? Good job!

Immersion into the subconscious is dangerous and often unnecessary. What is hidden down there, should not be set free. This... Well, there is no use trying to describe it. You will understand it soon.

You have an advantage. Your Spark is tempered, the blood of the Dragon flows in your veins, and the Irdrich story left a mark on your mind. Perhaps, the Planar Rim will be your entry point... The more familiar pictures, the better.
h: Ask about the surgery on your mind.

t: Your face is seen all over the city...
Ask Klavdia Kalugina in the Observatory how to get rid of Nihaz's influence.

All of it is curious. All the spirits, local gods, ancient devices, a light-bearing demon... But how should this help to banish Nihaz from your head? You should pick this bone with Klavdia, I guess.

She's a smart-pants, you can't hide things like this from her. Just tell her as it is. She might come up with a solution.
You again? All right, spit it out.

I've been waiting for you to come. I thought, it was impossible for the biggest cluck of this world to ignore the God of Darkness in their head for over a month!

But it was. And you did. But here you are, at last.

What am I doing here? Your Centaur story inspired me to take a look at Umoir... They're not fond of orcs, of course, but sheer League patriots are nowhere to be seen, either. They've got their own issues with the Leper, why would they care about the war?

Go on, tell me the whole story.

God or not God... An idea... it's too complicated. Who needs complicated? This piece of crap attacked Ammer with its golem, and he was beaten. He attacked Sogot, and he was beaten again, by demons and skinny scientists!

There's nothing special about him. Just another enemy.

What matters, is that he got lost from your brain. Let's drink for it.
Find a way to get rid of Nihaz's control over your mind.

First of all, I hate that all these things are happening on Sogot. Why couldn't Nihaz pull off this trick before? Is he the God of Darkness or what? I mean, he's Almighty, after all. Perhaps, there's something on Sogot that helped him. I'd like to sniff it out myself, but it's not that easy with all the demonologists and demons around.

Second, we have a god at our disposal. It's the Sculptor. He should know at least something about any divine laws of magic. You know, a vague idea. He kind of owes you, so you can shake him down for answers.

Third, it's the ginger-haired girl. Klavdia suggests she has a history with Nihaz, and it sounds a lot like yours. She might have an easy way out. I just didn't get it, whether Nihaz sent you for her, or you helped her escape from Nihaz... Or both? You can deal with it without me.

In the meantime, I'll talk to Zayan and Cosmos. The Great Mages might have a trick up their sleeve.
No news, cap, I'm afraid. What about you?
No news, cap, I'm afraid. What about you?
Ask Skulnar the Fierce about the demonic curse.

There's no use beating about the bush... I've been thinking about your nightmares back on Sogot... If he can make you do things that easily, someone might find it best to put you down...

We don't want them to do so, right? We don't. Listen now.
We're short of gods, so we have to get by, huh.
Skulnar the Fierce met by the Observatory on Dionic Archipelago
Skulnar obviously didn't have a chance to learn how to right properly. He scribbled you a very short note saying he would like to meet you near the Observatory.
All right, here comes! How are you doing, cap?

In short, there is a problem. They say Cosmos is making arrangements regarding this whole situation with Nihaz.

But I see things aren't going well for you. Why, you ask? It's the way you look. Wouldn't think you're the Hero of Sarnaut, hah.

You ought to... beef up, maybe? No, I'm not talking about pumping iron. I mean heroic deeds. Like helping our friends here.  I'll tell you where to go and what to do.

Once you help them, you'll be worthy of the title. And then you can go to Cosmos, and we'll think of how to defeat Nihaz.
Well, everything seems to be in order. Now get to Cosmos, quick. Time is pressing!
Meet Skulnar the Fierce near the Well of Souls on Ammer.
Skulnar obviously wasn't taught to write properly. He scribbled you a very short note saying he would like to meet you near the Well of Souls.
There you go. Well... How are you feeling, Cap?
Destiny is a dreadful thing, my friend.

This Smack the Lakefolk thinks too highly of himself! Snap, our previous chief, was no piece of cake... It isn't my fault, but I must clean up this mess.

If you think the Lakefolk made friends with us right after you killed Snap, think again. If they were a little more flexible, we could fight off the pirates together.

Tegorah's voice reverberates through your mind.

"We've managed to push most of the Destroyers back, but they're still trying to get to the lower levels of the Citadel. Please go down there and drive them out."
Tegorah looks at you questioningly. He is waiting to hear that the Destroyers have been banished.

The Archdemon inclines his head approvingly.

“This should stop them for a time. But more will follow...”
Eliminate the Destroyers in the Citadel.

Tegorah's voice reverberates through your mind.

"Destroyers. The scum of our race. Pathetic slaves of Nihaz, the mortal enemy of Sarn who created us. They are pure evil.

And this evil still threatens the Citadel. They need to be dealt with."
Tegorah gives you a questioning look. He is waiting to hear that the Destroyers have been banished from the Citadel.

The Archdemon inclines his head approvingly.

"Another attack rebuffed... But they will come again. Through time and space. Creating a future where we all have no place. Stop them."

Tegorah is silently looking at you. You can feel his inner anger, as if a room were filled with suffocating smoke. However, the demon is holding it together. An intricate hand gesture, and a vial filled with black and blue... substance appears in his hand out of the blue. Tegorah silently hands it to you and turns away.

Tegorah stays silent for a while. You can feel a light heat and awful itch. It translates from the demonic mental language as deep irritation. The archdemon seems to be out of sorts.

Nevertheless, his voice sounds extremely polite, although cool, when he starts to speak.

"Stormbringer, you're wondering if there are your enemies amongst us, demons. I can't blame you. I don't know anyone of my kin that matches your description".
h: Ask if there's a mage or a demon on Sogot that can affect other creatures' mind.

t:
...Tegorah silently hovers above the floor, absorbed in his thoughts. You feel the aura of power wrapped around the demon, but the power is... unusual. There is no chaos, no destructive energy hidden in it.

Just a strange unshakable confidence, like a crystal rock among the stormy astral. You are surprised to catch yourself bowing your head slightly in the Archdemon's presence. No wonder the demon is the leader of the local pack... If even the mortals sense the aura of his authority.

...Tegorah nods silently, and then you feel as though you are falling. For a moment, you think you are going to faint again, but the sensation fades as quickly as it appears. The Archdemon continues to look at you, but this time you begin to distinguish the echoes of emotions in his eyes. One is brighter than others: it's weariness. His weariness burns so bright that you can feel its heat.

Tegorah takes a step back, and the suffocating sensation goes away. The Archdemon bows his head as though apologizing. His voice echoes in your head.

"Forgive me for the inconvenience, Stormbringer. We will have to speak in this manner. These walls have eyes and ears."

The Archdemon bows his head, observing your reaction.

"Your nickname means nothing good. We cling to any good tidings, but the situation appears to be desperate. We have just been informed that the Destroyer broke into the upper platform. There will be slaughter. I will gladly answer any of your questions, but right now my attention is focused on the defense."
h: The aoidos sent me here to help.

t:
...The demon beckons you closer as though to whisper in your ear, but instead places a hand on your forehead. You instinctively tense, but the demon exudes no hostility. His hand does not feel warm or cold, or... alive. The next moment you realize that you no longer feel it, and what is more, you have completely lost the sense of your own body. As though neither of you exists separately - there is just one integral "I". Then the demon's consciousness unfolds before you like a book, and a flood of memories overwhelms you. You sense that the demon is hurriedly easing that flow lest you drown in this sea of information.

"The Demonologists crave power, Stormbringer. They wish to draw it from us. We had no choice other than to accept their "help". Without them, we'd have no shelter, and the advocates of Light would have wiped us out. The aoidos are our loyal allies, but they stand no chance against this world... They are like children."

...Tegorah sighs heavily. You see the entire Sogot before you. It takes you a while to realize that you are looking at the allod through the eyes of a flying demon.

"Everything has a price. We pay for their services with our powers and our lives. Both sides are fine with this arrangement. These lives are sacrificed for the good of all others. And yet... With the arrival of the Destroyers and servants of Light, many of us have been dying for nothing."

We don't know where the Destroyers came from. They are demons like us, yet they ignore our appeals. The only thing that drives them is their need to... destroy.
Ask demon hunters and representatives of the Church about the situation and find Skulnar the Fierce.

Here’s the medical history: you lapsed into a coma after the mess on the White Hook. I found no anomalous antibodies in your organism. The temperature is normal. After hearing your friends’ accounts, I concluded that you are suffering from two conditions: concussion caused by the demon rudely dropping you on your head, and chronic sleep deprivation.

And before you ask, being unconscious for more than a day doesn’t fix the second problem. You must keep in bed.

Still, you’ll need to meet the messengers of the Servants of the Light. Maya wants everyone to please them. And they seem to be concerned about your well-being. Why is that?

You have weird dreams... No, I didn’t peek. You’re just very talkative. Good morning, anyway.

I don’t like this place. Hell knows what’s happening here. Everyone keeps to themselves, staring at each other suspiciously. They don’t trust anyone, and that’s wise... The Trinity doesn’t help either. The Hunter is dumb as a fish, and the elf is wacky.

You should probably talk to the main demon. He’s a scary one, though if he decides to bite your head off, he’ll be honest about it. His name is Tegorah. Maybe he’ll tell you something useful?

And yes, these corridors are really confusing. Don’t be afraid - if you get lost, I’ll mount an expedition and come get you, heh.

...Tegorah turns to you. You feel like you are being placed on giant scales and measured. The Archdemon’s stare seems to look right at your Spark.

The echo of the demon’s emotion washes over you like a sea wave over cliffs. He seems to be... satisfied?

“You appear to be healthy. We could use your help.”
Defeat the Destroyers on the upper platform and inform Velit Molotov of your success.

Ah, there you are. You don’t consider those deadly metal things “peaceful” demons, do you? Great. Let’s go hunting.

I don’t need trophies and I don’t need your bluster. Just show them that demons aren’t welcome in this world. Our trust in the Light and swords will make short work of any vermin! They will pay tenfold for every drop of our blood!
Well, you know how to fight. I’m not surprised. If we could knock some sense into your head, you’d make a fine hunter.
Find and eliminate three powerful Destroyers on Sogot. Inform August de Grandeur of your success.

Ah, there you are. Wonderful! I was hoping I’d catch you before you run off to your next battle...

You see, we have wasted no time since arriving at the allod... Hunters’ scouts have been trying to determine the main sources of filth... Aside from the one we’re in, of course. Destroyers form packs just like any other demons, and they are headed by a powerful leader.

And that leader is just one demon.

We are clearly a minority here, so I suggest we move with minimum effort and maximum efficiency. We have located three especially powerful epicenters of the Destroyer forces and identified three leaders. Here are their descriptions. If you handle them, you’ll decapitate the whole armada and give us a head start as we prepare our counterattack. Sounds good, eh?
If you handle them, you’ll decapitate the whole armada and give us a head start as we prepare our counterattack. Sounds good, eh?

Good. I don’t like seeing people’s efforts go to waste... Especially since they paid for that information with their lives.

As you may have already guessed, our duties are different from whatever healers typically do... What’s the point in sending some fana... believers here? Anyway, thank you for your assistance. The Light shines brighter today.
Maya Voronina asked you to collect connecting amulets from the dead demons on the battlefield.

Good morning! Unfortunately, there was no time for formalities before, and the current situation is far from... I guess you have already met Tegorah. He’s quite a charismatic leader. It’s an important quality these days... Especially for a demon.

Let’s get down to business. I heard you’re heading for the frontline. Normally, I wouldn’t want to bother you with any requests, but this is a special occasion...

You see, every demon at the Citadel wears a special amulet. I registers and records anomalous activity in their organisms. Reactions to new irritants, fluctuations of astral energy... and the demon’s collapse at the time of their death. Our demons are dying on the frontline right now. Their deaths are a priceless material for research. We can’t let it go to waste!

I’d like you to collect these amulets from the bodies of the fallen before they are crushed in the heat of battle.

Wonderful... Every amulet is worth its weight in gold. All the demon’s memories and a great deal of his power... Yes, amulets absorb their energy as well. It would be useful after the death of our wards. A very useful invention.

At any rate, you’ve rendered me a great service. I won’t forget it.
Use Sarbaz Sais’s artifact against the Destroyers.

Wait a second... I need to ask you something.

You see, I’ve always been interested in the way Light could be used in technomagic. It’s one of the reasons I ended up joining the Church. And I have good grounds for believing that I’m close to completing my research!

Here, take this artifact. It’s a weakened version of my prototype. Weakened because it’s dangerous to trust a stranger with a technomagical device, especially if the power of said device largely depends on its bearer’s faith. All you need to do is test it on the Destroyers. Technically, it works against all demons, but if I were you, I wouldn’t aim it at our, ahem, “friends”. It may cause spontaneous combustion and misunderstanding...
If I were you, I wouldn’t aim it at our, ahem, “friends”. It may cause spontaneous combustion and misunderstanding...

Testing in field conditions was successful! Music for my dead ears.

Thank you very much. I can start adjusting it now.
Set up Nogrom’s defensive turrets on the Citadel’s upper platform.

I’ve built a few toys from bits and pieces. Let’s set them up on the platform, might even hit someone. I mean, you go set them up, I’m not going up there.

How? It’s easy! Just place them somewhere, press the big red button, wait until it unfolds, and the kick it for good measure. Works like a charm - Nogrom’s honor!
I hear the wonderful sounds of a shoot-out! So my babies work as expected. Let’s hope I set the correct target designation.
Retrieve Nogrom’s belongings and important parts of the ship from the shipwrecked Callisto at the White Hook.

Great, chief! Are you hurt? Okay, good.

I’ve been planning a trip to our ship, but the iron imps decided to attack us. Can’t sneak past them... Hm...

Yes, I need some stuff from my ship. The locals complain that the Citadel has no defenses to speak of. Hah! We’ll set some up easily as soon as I get my tools and supplies back. They don’t even have a proper workshop here! But that’s fine, we’ll manage...

Hey, maybe you and Skulnar can grab a few things?

So... Cannon ball... grenades... good! The drone is intact! I was afraid they’d explode before they let you catch them... What? What box? Ah, it exploded. Oh well. I don’t even remember what was inside.
Complete the quests at the Citadel to repel the demons’ attack.

...The Archdemon raises his staff belligerently. The heavy shaft strikes against the stone floor, and you glimpse faces of those who volunteered to defend the Citadel.

“Our differences can wait, Stormbringer. As long as we have a common enemy, and they are on our doorstep, no one will dare attack my demons... or Demonologists. I extend the same courtesy to our guests, and I expect the same of you. Insubordination will be punished by execu... I mean, law.

Take your weapon and face our enemies. Remind them why the whole world is afraid of you!”

...It seems as though sunlight is flooding the room. In the end, you realize it’s just triumph and pride radiating from Tegorah.

“The Destroyers have been pushed back!”
Obey the strict healer and go to bed

What the hell is this?!

What did I tell you? Bed! Rest!

Let’s start again. Perhaps there has been some misunderstanding. Bed rest means resting in bed. You get up only when you absolutely have to. Otherwise there will be insurmountable complications incompatible with life. In which case I will be executed for criminal negligence.

Go to bed. Now!
Wake up, sleepyhead! We have a problem.
Find Nogrom in the Citadel of Sogot.

What do you think... We were attacked last night. The guard was slaughtered, fortifications shredded. They even got inside and wrecked more havoc. At least they managed to sound the alarm...

You know, you’re looking a bit pale. Did you sleep well? No? Well, no wonder, with the stuff that’s happening... We’ll have you back on your feet in no time! Here, open this flask. Take a big swig. I’m not telling you what’s inside until you drink. Come on, drink!

What do you think? Hah, you bet! Pure glacial water. Direct from Ferris. You thought there’d be something nasty? Right, stereotypes! Put something on and let’s go find Nogrom. It’s gonna be a long day.

Yeah, I hear they broke through. Of course, they did. We have pitiful defenses...

But I intend to put an end to this outrage, hehe.

Those Destroyers decided for some reason that wearing chunks of strange metal was a good idea. Right! I opened tin cans with my teeth before I could walk, so these aren’t a challenge at all! Interaction with metals widens all sorts of horizons!

Look what I’ve made from bits and pieces. Stasis field generators? Easy. Homing mines? Done. Alarm system? Working on it - it’s incinerating instead of, well, alarming for some reason. Demon disintegrators? Here they are, my babies! And all in one night. I’m great, right? Right.

Sleep? That’s excessive. I’ve slept this month already.

There’s just one problem. We need to power all this stuff. And we’re really short of batteries. And there are no battleships parked nearby, so I can’t steal any! But I have an idea. Listen!
Get dressed and let’s go, cap'n. No time to waste! I’ll tell you the rest in the meantime.
Explore the Master's Citadel on the Isle of Revelation and collect the necessary data for Nogrom.

We need to break through that Citadel’s defenses and see what’s inside. You should ask that girl for help. The redhead who’s Veronica on Mondays and Berenika on Fridays. Apparently no one’s told her about other weekdays.

Here’s a scanner and here’s a crowbar. Crowbar is for those curious about your honest investigation. Don’t use it on anything in the Citadel! Even if you really want to.

Is everything clear? On with it, then!
Alright, get out of my workshop! The genius will awake soon, I need to make everything ready! But if you get me something to eat, I’ll be much obliged.
Examine the Heart of the Master’s Citadel.
...Numerous panels and lights blur and double before your eyes. Time to remember Nogrom’s instructions...
...You have retrieved all available data. Time to come back before the maniacal healer notices the absence of his favorite patient.

Weren’t you prescribed bed rest? Go now before stick mustard plasters on you, hehe.

I’ll pass, I think. They say you have unhealthy dreams here. I have better things to do than watch some silly nonsense.

Wake up, wake up! Creatures attacked our workshop!

Nogrom is nowhere to be found!

Wake up, wake up! Creatures attacked our workshop!

Nogrom is nowhere to be found!
You heard right! The local idiots slept through an army traipsing all over them. The workshop is wrecked. No one knows where Nogrom is. Alright, let’s go see it for ourselves!

My condolences, Stormbringer. Although... It seems rather strange, no?

We went to great lengths to ensure we had proper defenses. We strengthened our known weak points, launched a successful counterattack with minimal losses. And yet, when the night fell, all our efforts turned out to be in vain.

And the situation keeps reoccurring!
Wait until Zakhar Krestov finishes reading the messages.
Alright, let’s have a look at it. Since you’re a designated messenger, I may need you to take something back.
Oh, what a mess... Things are coming to a head!

Let’s start with that duo: Velit and Sais. We should ask them for a report on their mission. They will be forced to confirm the truth - that the Demonologists and demons fought shoulder to shoulder with them against the Destroyers. Let’s see how they are going to play this. We’ll also find out what they know about August.
I’m glad to see you. Can’t even round the corner - what if the Destroyers are there... Your timing is perfect.
Find August de Grandeur’s belongings on the upper platform and bring them to Sarbaz Sais.

Statement? Oh, Light... I’m afraid there won’t be much. I wasn’t on the upper platform yesterday, so I didn’t fight the Destroyers with the rest of the defenders. My statement is worth nothing. But I know someone who can tell you a lot!

August de Grandeur. Yes, you’re correct - he should have resurrected a while ago. However... The elf is nowhere to be found. I suggest you collect his belongings from the place where he died - since that night, it has been impossible to get to the upper platform, so they should still be there. I can carry out a special ritual to find out if August is around, or... if something is keeping him in the world of the dead.
I can carry out a special ritual to find out if August is around, or... if something is keeping him in the world of the dead.
So what do we have here? His lamp, his blood... A picture locket... who’s Franz de Vevre? Oh, fine. Let’s get on with it.
Drink the deadly poison and find the spark of August de Grandeur in Purgatory.

Just a second... Ah, damnation...!

Please forgive me. The reaction is too unexpected. And anomalous, too... No, August is not among the living. Do you understand? The Destroyer killed a true believer, and he can’t resurrect! It sounds like we don’t have a choice.

We need to find his spark in Purgatory and find out what happened.

Here, take it. It’s a deadly poison. You know what to do. See you on the other side.

The procedure is far from pleasant, I agree... And we didn’t learn much. Just the fact that August de Grandeur is irreversibly dead, which changes a few things... Well, I’m ready to give my statement.
Find Velit Molotov and clear the wing of the demons along the way.

Me? Dead? No way.

Well, yes, it was a scary creature, I barely escaped. And the notes... Like that's gonna happen! I'm alive and keeping busy. I found your Molotov. He's in the next wing. But there are lots of demons here and the passage is blocked.

How about this: you kill demons, I blow things up. And never mind the explosions, we're in a hurry. Okay?
You’re right on time! There is a problem...
Hold off the Destroyers while the Demonologists are sealing the breach in the wall.
The imps just keep coming! We must seal this breach - can’t leave it gaping like this. But I can’t protect workers and kill demons at the same time... Lend a hand, will you?
Phew... That was close... If it wasn’t for you, we’d all be dead.
You need my statement... Can do. I saw everything I needed to see. Let me get my bearings first. I'm not used to writing.
Let me get my bearings first. I’m not used to writing.
There it is. So, the seal... You can take it to Zakhar. He probably won’t be happy, but he’s never happy. The old man is always grumbling about something...
Gather evidence about the Demonologists' actions and show it to Zakhar Krestov on Black Spit.

You can’t imagine the level of preparation and alertness after that fiasco. No mouse should be able to sneak by unnoticed, let alone an army. And yet... The Citadel is swarming with enemies. The snake is right in our heart.

It sounds like we have a rat. And I can’t help but think that everything that’s happening benefits the Church. Just think about it: any fight between us and the Destroyers serves their interests. They exhaust both sides... August de Grandeur should have already resurrected. Something tells me these tricks are right up his alley.

Well, let’s continue our diplomatic efforts... If our luminous friends are trying to gather evidence against us to avoid direct orders from on high, we’ll go the opposite way. We’ll work with these worrywarts and prove our innocence.

Aggressively.
So, you’re alive and well? Good to know. Are there no other messengers in this hotbed of heresy?
Tell Skulnar about the situation and check with the healer.

Well, come on, then. Tell me what you were thinking. Were you out of your mind? Trying to pull demons away from the camp? Hijacking a ship? What did you activate there, anyway? My eyes still hurt, and I didn’t even look at it!
Fine... the goblin is not completely useless. His signal mines have been activated, see? We’re going to have guests soon.
Help fortify the camp by building barricades and repairing Nogrom’s cannon

No rest for you, sleeping beauty! We’re going to have guests soon, and we should give them a warm welcome!

The ship has been scrapped, we are building barricades! Just nail the planks down... Nogrom is working on something, maybe we’ll even have artillery. But barricades should com first! Come on, cap'n, shake a leg before they toss us into astral!

So you’re an experienced astral traveler, right? Get behind the cannon and pull the trigger! I did my job and built it, but I have no idea how to aim it!!

Goodness, they are flying in! Kill them!
That was a hard fight! They knew when to attack...
Broker a truce between the Demonologist leader and the chief Demon Hunter.

Oh, I don’t like this... Iron demons weren’t enough for these soldiers - now they’re trying to kill each other... What do we do?

Maybe we should... brainwash them? No? Alright, fine. You go talk to them, then. Diplomatically! But don’t be afraid to be expressive either. That Xadaganian girl is the leader of the Demonologists, apparently. And that Kanian is clearly the chief hunter.

Good luck.
Ah, the patient deigned to awaken. Aren’t you tired of malingering? It’s been two days. Yes, our sanctuary is full of... strangers thanks to you.
We are the order of the Demonologists, and this land belongs to the Citadel! The Hunters have trespassed on our territory and attacked us!
Of course they won’t - we have demons like that for breakfast! How can you protect demons whey have just tried to kill everyone? Demons are evil, and they must be eradicated!
h: These demons want to live peacefully. They won't hurt you.

t:
I hear you caused a ruckus the past couple of nights. Have you no shame, doing it in someone else’s house? The poor elf is afraid of you even in the afterlife, and you nearly killed your friend! Yes, with your own hands...

Ha ha ha! That look on your face is priceless!

I own you now. Deal with it.
I own you now. Deal with it.
Come, child, bathe in the rivers of blood. Daddy doesn’t mind.

Oh? I’ll have to disagree! You think my assistant just scratched you?

Well, no. Your body is just cosmic dust. Simple matter. Power over matter is my prerogative, you see.

So listen. There will be a battle in your Citadel. I won’t lie to you, that’s exactly what I’ve been waiting for... but those believers are way too zealous, even for me! I’ve always said there’s nothing more dangerous than fanatics.

Their eyes are glowing with the flames of a right cause! They ooze righteousness! Self-proclaimed judges with delusions of grandeur! Such people are so easy to manipulate.

You’ll kill them all, one by one. They outlived their usefulness. Just imagine the conversations it would provoke: the Demonologists subjugated Destroyers and flooded the fields of Sogot with blood! I can even restore life here after such an occasion. Blood-red trees, shrubs with bloody berries... Snow white rabbits with scarlet eyes hopping on crimson grass...

Idyll!
h: You have no power over me!

t:
That's it? No resistance? Excellent!

So listen. There will be a battle in your Citadel. I won't lie to you, that's exactly what I've been waiting for... but those believers are way too zealous, even for me! I've always said there's nothing more dangerous than fanatics.

Their eyes are glowing with the flames of a right cause! They ooze righteousness! Self-proclaimed judges with delusions of grandeur! Such people are so easy to manipulate.

You'll kill them all, one by one. They outlived their usefulness. Just imagine the conversations it would provoke: the Demonologists subjugated Destroyers and flooded the fields of Sogot with blood! I can even restore life here after such an occasion. Blood-red trees, shrubs with bloody berries... Snow white rabbits with scarlet eyes hopping on crimson grass...

Pure harmony!
h: Yes, Master. I’ll do as you say...

t:
...Desire to kill the orc flares like a fire in a dry forest. You see your own arm rise but you are helpless to stop it. A Destroyer's mind knows no fear or mercy. The orc does not back down, however. He comes at you with his arms open as though intending to embrace you.

The next instant his voice explodes in your mind, paralyzing your body - the alien body - with unbearable pain.

"Stop!"

...It is an order you are happy to obey. Skulnar comes closer, and you feel his unquestionable power over the demon's mind. His days in the Laboratory were not spent in vain. You hear the orc's voice from afar, as though there is a wall of water between you.

"An entire Citadel full of demons and "Demonologists", damn them, and none of them sensed there's something wrong with you...

You. Come. With me!"

...You obediently take a step forward.

This is it... Don’t worry, we’ll find a way to get you out. I’ll have Cosmos’s head if need be.

Now here’s what you’re going to do...

There’s only one thing we can do - take out that crazy Zem before she gets us all killed. Destroyers are against us, so you’ll crush her as a Destroyer. That way no one will complain that the local demons or warlocks are against the Light.

Got it? Find Sarbaz Sais! Stop her! Kill her if need be! If you see our people on the way - help them, but don’t linger too long! Go now!
Ah, hm... Of course I knew the weapon would do this... No side effects or unwanted deaths. Goblin’s honor, right. So that creature ate you?

Ah, so Skulnar thought of everything, apparently, and I... made a bit of a mess.

But who cares? The Citadel is going to blow up any minute now! This lunatic wants to free the Heart of the Citadel and reload the generators. That demon is the Heart! She must be stopped, and if the believers start complaining - deal with them next! Right?

Come on, while there’s still time! Perhaps I can stabilize the systems if she hasn’t destroyed them...

What in the name of Chaos is going on here?!

How did you get here?

Ah. Never mind. We repelled the attack. It wasn’t easy, but we did it. We haven’t lost many demons, but the Demonologists... Let’s say things could have gone better. Much better.

Some of the Hunters helped us fight. Probably after their leader recklessly killed Molotov. Velit will resurrect, but Zakhar... Some demon tore him apart. Good riddance.

And now the highlight of today’s show... The cleric. We can’t judge her - there’ll be a scandal. But you have a perfect right to do it... Since the Great Mage himself bestowed that authority on you.
We can’t judge her - there’ll be a scandal. But you have a perfect right to do it.
We got rid of that vermin, which is good. Let’s get out of here, shall we?

I’m not flying anywhere with this lot again. I’d rather use portals, even though they give me indigestion... Portals aren’t working now, though... apparently, something broke after one lousy goblin decided to bring down a whole section of the Citadel, together with an armada of Destroyers... Yeah... Good times.

We’ll get out of here tomorrow. Sorry, cap’n, but I’ll be guarding your cot tonight. Just in case.

Don’t thank me, heh.

Well, the Demonologists got what they wanted. After what happened, the Church will think twice before challenging us. As for the demons... Their alliance with the Demonologists will lead to no good. But that’s their life and their choice.

We can only wish them luck.

What do you mean? You’re like Cairage. Blind and dumb. Though Cairage at least had the sense to stay out of sight... Until later. Believe it or not, he’s sitting right there, under our feet. Underneath Sogot. Quiet as a mouse, hearing every word spoken at the Citadel. Every step, every sound of a dead body hitting the ground.

Your hearing improves if you spend thousands of years blind, you know.

I think I’ll have to drag him out to the surface. Such power cannot be left unchecked.
h: Why are you telling me this?

t: Tell Milas aboard the Callisto that you are ready to leave for Sogot

I hear it’s an emergency. We should leave immediately - there’s an astral storm coming our way, so it’s better if we leap through before it the sky turns upside down.

My guys are ready. Give the word, Stormbringer.
I see you’re still capable of thinking. How are you feeling? We crashed...

It's bad. The ship was dragged through these... bones? Through half of the allod. There's nothing left of her. Or her captain, which is especially tragic! You see, no one's waiting for his kind in Purgatory.

They are all panicking now. We must do something! Use your commanding tone! I'm only good at screaming. Or brainwashing, but that would be inhumane. Look, just find out what they're fussing about.
Look, just find out what they’re fussing about.
Captain! Just make them shut up.
I’ll look around. Perhaps some of our supplies survived the crash.
h: Order to prepare food using whatever ingredients they can find.

t: There are bones and weird flowers all over the place. What should we cook with?
I’ll get it done. Who knows when those demons come back... I’ll gather everyone who can fight.
h: Order to gather the strongest crew members and equip them for patrol and defense.
Render first aid to the wounded.

t: Give the Aoidoi instructions at the wreck site and return to Skulnar the Fierce.

Let’s not sit idly - we aren’t chickens. Give some tasks to your crew. Me and Nogrom will decide on a course of action.

We need to get out of here somehow, and the little guy is smarter than he looks. He might think of something.
Keep your crew busy. Me and Nogrom will decide what to do next.

You’re a born leader!

I’ll keep an eye on them, and you go talk to Nogrom. He’s got an idea, I think.
Meet Nefer Ur on the platform near the Observatory on Ammer.

...The infocube unfolds in your hands, its tiny steel elements fitting into hidden slots, making you wonder at the technology. In the end, a small pedestal is formed in your palm, with a greenish hologram of the Great Mage of the Arisen appearing on it. Nefer Ur's hands are resting behind his back; his porcelain mask shows no emotion. The Great Mage raises his head slightly, and his eyes meet yours. You hear his voice as though it is coming from inside your head...

"Circumstances require your involvement. The matter has nothing to do with the League or the Empire. The aoidos and their new... allies need your help. I have a vested interest in this as well. Meet me near the Observatory on Ammer. Make haste."

...Sounds urgent.
Thank you for your quick response.
Ask Nefer Ur about his problem.

It’s not my problem. It’s the problem of demons and their allies, the Aoidoi. I’d rather the Aoidoi never encountered such unpleasant problems.

Tell me what you know about the Demonologist order?

You see, Stormbringer, we’d like to provide assistance to the demons. More than anything in the world. But we’re not allowed to interfere! Nefer Ur told us about the looming political conflict and war... War against us! However righteous our intentions, we will not let our people die for them.
I am concerned about the future of demons, because we are the ones responsible for our alliance with them.
Talk to Captain Milas aboard the Callisto.

There is only one creature both Light worshippers and demons fear and respect. It’s you, Stormbringer.

I want to believe in Nefer Ur’s good intentions, but the man wouldn’t be in his position if he didn’t know how to benefit from anything that occurs in this world. I advise you to be careful with the Demonologists, my friend. Their methods are different from ours. They see demons as a tool... Nothing good can come from those who consider living creatures as a means of self-exaltation.

Sogot is a remote allod, so you’ll need a ship to travel there. We’ve gathered an expedition prepared for the long voyage. You see, Aoidoi aren’t very experienced astral travelers, but these people are better suited than others. The ship is already waiting for you.

Good luck, Stormbringer.

Ah, there you are.

Milas. Nice to meet you.

Interesting!

I got a letter. Addressed to you. Nefer Ur sent it.

I wonder what the Arisen wants?

Ah, if only you knew how long I've known him... But now is not the time to indulge in sentimental memories of Hickut. There's a package attached to the letter. It contains a curious thing - the Infocube.

Let's turn it on and see what he has to say.
Come on, turn it on! Don't make me wait. I'm dying of curiosity.
Ahaha! It's fortunate that you're here! I think it's time we talked.
What a dread. What Nihaz wants with me in the future? Anyway, he’s not getting it!
h: Tell about the Purgatory from the future

t: A good place to rest from the buzz of Polis.
